interpretation: It is impossible that the mover which is itself moved by another should go on to infinity, since among infinitely many there is no first (ἀδύνατον γὰρ εἰς ἄπειρον ἰέναι τὸ κινοῦν καὶ κινούμενον ὑπʼ ἄλλου αὐτό· τῶν γὰρ ἀπείρων οὐκ ἔστιν οὐδὲν πρῶτον). Formalized as well-foundedness of the link 'moves this thing, is another than it, and is itself moved by another'. Unlike the prima via's regress premise it is not restricted to per se links; the chapter's stick-hand-man example (256a6-13) illustrates it, and the per accidens case is taken up only from 256b3.
